-170.70000,-14.30000.name: 19-097-101r — Sss (Aventis)
-170.70000,-14.30000.size: 1 declared release location across 1 state, 3 acres
-170.70000,-14.30000.desc: Permit to release genetically engineered sss at 1 declared location in AS. Applicant: Aventis. Status: Issued. Declared traits: bacterial resistance. The applicant claimed confidential business information on this record, so the trait description is partly withheld as [CBI] in the source. The dot is scattered inside the state, not placed at a site: APHIS publishes the state and the number of release locations, never the locations themselves. Australia is the only regulator in the world that publishes field trial sites. Position is a state centroid, not the site — APHIS publishes release states, never coordinates.

-110.88300,32.24750.name: Arizona Center for Reproductive Endocrinology and Infertility
-110.88300,32.24750.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Timothy J. Gelety, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

100.34568,13.86109.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Department of Medical Sciences, Ministry of Public Health. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

144.96310,-37.81360.desc: The Australian university partnership working on thylacine de-extinction, funded by Colossal. Australian marsupial genomics is genuinely advanced by this work, whatever one makes of the goal, which is the recurring bargain in this facet: a spectacular target funds unglamorous capability that would otherwise go unfunded.

-71.04800,42.35400.name: Sarepta Therapeutics
-71.04800,42.35400.desc: Sells gene therapies for Duchenne muscular dystrophy approved on accelerated pathways over the objections of some FDA reviewers, at prices above three million dollars. Patient advocacy, regulator discretion and commercial interest converged on the same decision, and the confirmatory evidence arrived after the approval rather than before it.

4.76600,52.74200.name: Enza Zaden
4.76600,52.74200.desc: A Dutch vegetable breeder, family-owned, in the cluster of firms that dominate world vegetable seed. It has used editing in research while the EU treats edited plants as GMOs, which for a European breeder means the technique is available in the laboratory and not in the market — the position the proposed EU regulation would change.

173.26000,-35.10000.name: Ngāti Kuri, Ngāti Wai, Te Rarawa, Ngāti Porou, Ngāti Kahungunu and Ngāti Koata
173.26000,-35.10000.state: Aotearoa New Zealand — the six claimant iwi
173.26000,-35.10000.desc: The six iwi whose members lodged the claim in 1991 and pursued it for two decades. All six original claimant representatives died before the process concluded, and a sense of unfinished business has persisted since the report. This map records petitioners as well as tribunals because a finding requires someone willing to spend twenty years obtaining it, and the cost is not usually written down anywhere. Set beside the nine-year South African case, the twenty-year Indian petition and the two-year Costa Rican action, the pattern is consistent: the timescale of a challenge to genetic technology is measured in decades, and the technology moves considerably faster.

174.77700,-41.27900.name: Gene Technology Bill — ending New Zealand's outdoor ban
174.77700,-41.27900.desc: Recorded here as a bill rather than a law, which is the accurate state of it. It would end a nearly thirty-year restriction on genetically modified organisms outside the laboratory, moving gene technology out of the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996 into a standalone risk-tiered regime, and creating a Gene Technology Regulator: a statutory officer appointed by the minister, employed and supported by the Environmental Protection Authority, accountable to the EPA for employment and to the minister otherwise. The regulator could exempt technologies assessed as minimal risk or indistinguishable from conventional breeding. The government stated the model is closely based on Australia's Gene Technology Act 2000. The scale of the response is worth recording: the Health Committee received 14,458 written submissions and heard 287 oral submitters, reporting back on 10 October 2025. Objections on the record include the absence of any coexistence provision for conventional and organic growers, left to industry to resolve, and a confidentiality carry-over from HSNO that the Chief Ombudsman noted risks protecting information that ought to be released.
